title: Kimi Joins Forces with HuaSheng TianCheng, Kingsoft Cloud, and Other Giants to Enter the Core of Enterprises

content_html:
On September 10th, the unicorn large model company Moonshot AI officially announced the launch of the "Kimi Enterprise Partner Program," marking its large model technology beginning to fully advance into core enterprise business scenarios.

The core goal of this initiative is to provide enterprises with genuine AI implementation paths that deeply integrate into core business operations through ecosystem collaboration, and to focus on cultivating frontline deployment engineers (FDE) teams. As large models become more prevalent across industries, enterprises generally face the "last mile" challenge of implementation—how to deeply integrate model capabilities with their own business. To address this, Moonshot AI will comprehensively open up core support including model and Agent backends, solution accumulation, and capability transformation.

In terms of specific implementation models, Kimi adopts a highly open ecosystem collaboration strategy. Moonshot AI provides advanced model capabilities and mature engineering methodologies, while partners leverage their industry insights and customer service advantages. The two parties will combine strengths to jointly cultivate professional engineer teams,打通 the entire delivery process from demand diagnosis, solution design, to production deployment, ensuring AI can truly be transformed into enterprise productivity.

Currently, the program has already attracted the participation of the first batch of leading industry enterprises. Several well-known technology and service companies, including Huasheng Tiancheng,金山云 (Kingsoft Cloud), Yacong Co., Yaxin Technology, and China Software International, have officially joined as Kimi enterprise partners. This not only demonstrates Kimi's strong appeal in the enterprise market but also signals that the commercialization of AI large models in the B-end market will enter a new phase of accelerated development.
